intro: Before you stands Gümüşkesen Tomb, in Muğla province, from the 2nd century AD. This Roman tomb at Milas is taken to be a scaled-down copy of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, and its pyramid roof and colonnaded upper storey are still standing.
history: This two-storey tomb at Milas was built in the second century AD. Below lies a burial chamber; above, a colonnaded storey carries a pyramid roof. It is taken to be a scaled-down reading of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, a hundred kilometres away. That great building was stripped to its foundations, so it is Gümüşkesen that gives the clearest idea of the lost wonder.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the pyramid roof and the colonnaded upper storey. Then look into the burial chamber, and up at the ceiling decoration.
facts: Did you know? The opening in the middle of the burial chamber floor was cut so that liquids offered to the dead could run down into it. And the tomb is read as a scaled-down version of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus; since that building was stripped to its foundations, this tomb gives the clearest idea of the lost wonder.
outro: This brings our tour of Gümüşkesen Tomb to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This tomb has kept its shape for centuries; let it keep it for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
